theater: 太原郡晉陽縣（晉陽故城）

battle.name: 楊世洛起義
battle.theater: 太原郡晉陽縣（晉陽故城）
battle.brief: 大業十三年十月丁亥，太原人楊世洛聚眾萬餘人，攻城掠邑。時太原一帶已歸李淵次子李元吉節制，隋廷徵發未解、府兵久疲，起兵旬月即擾及鄰縣。兩《隋書》於此僅留一語，其後無詳。卡面羅馬重步兵並未入華，可與之對照者，是隋軍具裝步卒結重盾長槊之陣。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是楊世洛率領的起義眾，一方是控制太原郡的隋唐官軍。起義方以太原郡本地人為主體：大業年間連年徵兵留下的逃卒、逃戶，以及在屯田與軍糧徭役下失去生業的鄉里百姓，加上被裹挾的諸縣民眾，聚合在郡境內的村落、山地與城堡之間；《北史》卷十二與《隋書》卷四都只說「聚眾萬餘人，攻城掠邑」，並無記錄其編制、旗號與首領以下的指揮架構，可知者僅是他們足以在郡內同時威脅多縣，而非一支有軍籍、有編號的正規部隊。官軍一方則分兩層：隋室在太原郡設郡丞與縣吏，郡兵之外另有府兵、鄉兵與縣級團練，歸中央調度；自大業十三年五月李淵在晉陽起兵、七月進封唐王之後，太原郡實際由李淵第四子李元吉以隴西郡公節制，郡兵與縣兵的調度歸其幕府，更大範圍的軍務則由李建成以河東道行軍元帥領晉陽之師、李世民領關中兵馬策應。同年末，劉武周又與東突厥相應攻入太原，三套政權、三套指揮系統在河東互相重疊，太原郡成了事實上的真空地帶。
countriesEn: The two parties were the insurgents led by Yang Shiluo on one side and, on the other, the Sui-Tang official forces that held Taiyuan commandery. The rebel side was drawn almost entirely from the commandery's own people: deserters and runaway households left over by the endless levies of the Daye years, country folk whose fields and livelihoods had been destroyed by corvee and by the military transport of grain, and villagers of the neighbouring counties swept in along with them, gathered in the villages, hills and stockaded strongholds of the commandery. The History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 12, and the History of Sui, juan 4, record only that they 'gathered more than ten thousand men, attacked cities and plundered towns'; there is no account of their organisation, their banners, or any chain of command beneath their leader, so all that can be said is that they were numerous enough to threaten several counties of the commandery at once, and not that they were a numbered regular force with a military register. The official side worked in two layers. Under the Sui, Taiyuan had a commandery vice-magistrate and county officers, and besides the commandery troops there were registered soldier households, local levies and county militia, all answerable to the centre. After Li Yuan rose at Jinyang in the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Daye and was advanced to the title of Prince of Tang in the seventh month, the commandery in practice passed to Li Yuanji, Li Yuan's fourth son, who held it with the title of Prince of Longxi and a staff of his own, and the disposition of the commandery and county troops fell to that staff, while the wider war was directed by Li Jiancheng, who led the Hedong army as xingjun yuanshuai, and by Li Shimin, who commanded in Guanzhong and marched east to join them. At the end of the same year Liu Wuzhou, in concert with the Eastern Turks, entered Taiyuan, so that three polities with three chains of command lay over one another in Hedong and Taiyuan commandery had become in practical terms a vacuum.
people: 起義的首領是楊世洛。《北史》卷十二《隋本紀下》與《隋書》卷四《帝紀第四·煬帝下》都記：大業十三年十月丁亥，太原人楊世洛聚眾萬餘人，攻城掠邑。《北史》於姓名用了一個異體的寫法，兩史所記的日期、地點、人數卻完全一致。兩書都沒有寫他的官職或部曲之眾，反應他憑的是民間號召臨時聚起，組織鬆散，對縣治的攻擊隨起隨伏，沒有定式的兵陣。其時主持太原軍政的是李淵的第四子李元吉。太原郡既是李淵起兵的根基，也是李氏軍隊兵源與糧秣的所在，李元吉自起兵之初便以隴西郡公的身份留鎮太原，督理郡兵與屯田；楊世洛起事，使他一面要分兵彈壓郡內亂源，一面要防備同年冬天劉武周引突厥兵入塞。稍早於此，李建成以河東道行軍元帥屯晉陽，李世民則領兵在關中，平定渭北與隴右，並於同年冬引兵東返會盟；三人各掌一路，楊世洛這樣一支地方起義隊伍，正是在這樣的權力真空與兵力分散之間坐大。隋方此役的主將姓名，諸史皆未記載，這一點本身說明此役在正史眼中只是邊角之事。
peopleEn: The man who headed the rising was Yang Shiluo. The History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 12, Annals of Sui part two, and the History of Sui, juan 4, Emperor Yang part four, both record that in the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Daye, on the dinghai day, Yang Shiluo of Taiyuan gathered more than ten thousand men and attacked cities and plundered towns. The History of the Northern Dynasties writes his name with a variant form of the surname, but the two histories agree exactly on the date, the place and the numbers. Neither of them gives him an office, a rank or any body of retainers, which shows that he had rallied a following among ordinary people, hastily assembled and loosely organised, whose attacks on the county seats began and broke off as the mood took them, with no set battle order. The man holding military authority in Taiyuan was Li Yuanji, Li Yuan's fourth son. Taiyuan commandery was the foundation of Li Yuan's rising and the place from which the Li family's soldiers and grain were drawn, and Li Yuanji had remained there as Prince of Longxi from the first days of the revolt, supervising the commandery troops and the garrison farms. The rising of Yang Shiluo obliged him at once to detach men to put down the disturbance inside the commandery and at the same time to guard against Liu Wuzhou, who brought Turkic forces across the frontier in the winter of that same year. Shortly before this Li Jiancheng had been stationed at Jinyang as xingjun yuanshuai of Hedong, while Li Shimin had led troops in Guanzhong, pacifying Weibei and Longyou, and in the winter of the same year marched east to the meeting; each of the three brothers held a separate command, and it was precisely in such a condition of divided authority and scattered troops that a local rising of Yang Shiluo's kind could grow. The name of any Sui commander at this action is preserved in none of the histories, and that silence in itself shows how far the affair stood from the centre of the official record.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬重步兵，設計年代約在公元前一百年前後，是羅馬共和晚期至帝國早期重步兵的標準形象：分段結構的鎧甲、一面可遮住大半身的大盾，配短劍與長矛。卡面所附的說明是「分段鎧甲配重盾」，重點不在甲胄本身，而在羅馬的戰力來源——靠徵兵制在兵源枯竭時不斷補充兵員，靠屯田與糧道維持遠征部隊的補給，所以重甲部隊在正面會戰中極耐打，卻從不單獨作戰。裝備細節也說明這一點：鎧甲分段，便於修理與逐件更換；重盾與短劍適合密集線陣中的推擠與格鬥，而不是分散游鬥。卡面這件兵器從未出現在中國，更不曾出現在唐初的太原郡；此役雙方真正上手的，是隋唐軍系的步戰裝備。隋軍重步兵有明光鎧這類金甲與兜鍪，配漆木大盾，長兵器用槊與長刀；投射火器有角弓、臂弓與強弩，近身重擊靠槊刺與刀斫；騎兵著鐵甲，佩長刀與長槊，作戰時以數百至數千騎為一部，衝鋒之前先用弩箭消耗敵陣。野戰與攻城的輔助器材包括偏箱車、櫓車、拒馬、鹿角、撞車、巢車與雲梯，火則以火箭與火把為主，《隋書·兵車志》正是唐人編纂前代軍制的憑藉。從兵制上看，隋唐是府兵制：以戶為單位，兵將相離，番上宿衛與徵發並用，糧秣靠租庸調與轉運供給——這與羅馬靠兵源與補給線致勝的邏輯同源，兩者在末年都因供糧與徵兵失靈而崩壞。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a Roman heavy infantryman of about the year 100 BC, the standard image of the heavy infantry of the late Republic and early Empire: a segmented cuirass, a large shield covering most of the body, a short sword and a long spear. The note attached to the card reads 'segmented armour and heavy shield', and the real point lies not in the armour itself but in where Roman strength came from: a recruiting system that could replenish the manpower when it ran short, and settled farms and supply lines that could keep an army on campaign fed, which is why armoured formations were very hard to break in a pitched battle and yet never fought alone. The equipment tells the same story. Segmented plates could be repaired and replaced piece by piece, and the heavy shield with the short sword belonged to the push and grind of a close-packed line, not to loose skirmishing. The card's weapon never appeared in China and certainly never in the Taiyuan commandery of the early Tang; what the two sides actually handled here were the armaments of the Sui-Tang infantry system. The Sui heavy infantry had cuirasses of the shining-plate type, worn over a jacket, with iron helmets, and lacquered wooden shields, while their long weapons were the spear and the long sabre; their missile weapons were angle bows, arm bows and powerful crossbows, and their close work was done with the thrust of the spear and the stroke of the sabre. The horse was armoured in iron and carried the long sabre and the long spear, and a tactical unit of it was some hundreds to some thousands of riders who first exhausted the enemy line with crossbow bolts before charging. Auxillary materiel for the field and the siege included armoured waggons, mantlets, caltrops, abatis, battering rams, siege towers and scaling ladders, with fire supplied by fire-arrows and torches, and the History of Sui with its treatise on war carriages is the source, compiled by Tang hands, for this earlier military system. In terms of organisation, both Sui and Tang worked through the fubing system: soldiers were drawn from households, service alternated between garrison and field, and grain came from the poll tax and from transport. That is the same logic as the Roman reliance on manning and supply, and the two systems failed in the same way in their last years, when provisioning and recruitment broke down.
tactics: 起義方的打法，正史只留下「攻城掠邑」四字，但可從郡境地形與當時形勢推知其骨架。起兵於十月，正是秋收之後、冬耕之前，糧食可以支應，兵員也易於糾合；眾合萬餘，分成數股活動於汾河兩岸、晉陽周邊的縣城與鄉里之間，不必與官軍主力決戰，只求攻下縣城、掠取積粟與丁壯。太原郡的縣治多為中小城邑，縣兵殘缺、守備空虛，起義眾既佔人數之便，又有聚眾而來的聲勢，攻掠小城比攻大城容易，所以首波衝擊很可能落在鄰近的縣城，而非郡治晉陽城本身。官軍一方的應對則以守城與重點清剿為主：唐軍以晉陽為基地，用騎兵巡邏、據守城池、以小股兵卒各個擊破，避免與萬餘眾在野外交鋒；李元吉還須分兵防劉武周，兵力更形分散。地形上，太原在汾河谷地之中，四面有山，西南通河中的離石、永寧一線，東出井陘可達河北，糧秣仰給於汾河與晉陽的水陸轉運，這正是唐廷在此設留守的原因，也是起義眾能以劫掠就地取糧、維持數月的條件。史籍未載此役的具體會戰與攻城細節，以上只就已知的地勢與兵力對比作保守推斷。
tacticsEn: The method of the insurgents survives only in the four characters 'attacked cities and plundered towns', but its shape can be reconstructed from the terrain of the commandery and the situation of the day. The rising began in the tenth month, after the autumn harvest and before the winter ploughing, so that grain could be found and men could be got together; the more than ten thousand who gathered were split into several bodies active in the towns and villages on both banks of the Fen river and around Jinyang, and there was no need to offer battle to the main body of the government troops: the object was to carry off county seats and take the stored grain and the able-bodied men. Most of the county seats of Taiyuan commandery were small towns with thin garrisons and hollow defences, and a rebel mass that was stronger in numbers and imposing in appearance found it far easier to take a small town than a great one, so the first blows very likely fell on the neighbouring county towns rather than on Jinyang itself. The official side answered by holding the cities and clearing the countryside piece by piece: the Tang forces used Jinyang as their base, sent out patrols of horse, stayed behind walls and struck at the rebels in small detachments, and avoided meeting a mass of more than ten thousand in the open field; Li Yuanji moreover had to detach men to watch Liu Wuzhou, and his strength was scattered still further. The ground tells its part of the story. Taiyuan lies in the basin of the Fen river, ringed by mountains, with the road to Hedong and Guanzhong running south-west through Lishi and Yongning, and east through Jingxing towards the northern plains, while the grain came up the Fen and by water and road from Jinyang. That is precisely why the Tang court kept a resident commander there, and equally why the rebels could keep themselves for months by seizing grain on the spot. No history records the actual meetings and assaults of this action, so what is set out here is a conservative inference from the known terrain and the known strengths of the two sides.
data: 可引的數字極少，且都出自兩《隋書》的一句記載。時間：大業十三年十月丁亥，隋唐曆以十月為歲首，此月落在公曆六一七年十月至十一月之間。兵力：起義眾「萬餘人」，這是史籍給出的唯一人數概數；官軍投入的兵數、戰損、斬獲、攻下的城邑數目，諸史皆無記載，不宜編造。地理：太原郡領晉陽、太原、文水、交城、祁、太谷、榆次、汾陽、壽陽、盂、石艾、平城、樂平、和順、遼山十五縣，郡治晉陽在今太原市西南；起義「攻城掠邑」所及，應在此範圍之內。背景數字可作對照：大業七年至十三年，隋朝兩度征高句麗，史稱役丁動以百萬，役夫倍之，太原是出兵的基地與軍糧的來源之一；役後天災疫癘相隨，隋煬帝又於大業十二年冬第三次徵天下之兵於遼東，役死者填道餓殍遍野，太原一帶的民戶承受尤其直接。到了大業十三年，五月李淵起兵、七月進封唐王、年底劉武周入太原，及至武德二年隋煬帝死於江都的消息傳遍天下、隋室名存實亡，楊世洛起兵的時點正在這個秩序崩解的窗口裡。卡面那件兵器則更早，約公元前一百年前後的羅馬重步兵裝備，與此役無涉。
dataEn: Very few figures survive, and all of them come from a single sentence in the two Histories of Sui. The date: the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Daye, on the dinghai day; the Sui and Tang calendar made the tenth month the first month of the year, so the month falls between October and November of 617 in the Gregorian reckoning. The strength: 'more than ten thousand men' for the insurgents, the only head-count the histories give; the number of government troops engaged, the losses, the captures and the number of cities taken are all absent, and must not be invented. The geography: Taiyuan commandery governed fifteen counties, Jinyang, Taiyuan, Wenshui, Jiaocheng, Qi, Taigu, Yuci, Fenyang, Shouyang, Yu, Shiai, Pingcheng, Leping, Heshun and Liaoshan, with its seat at Jinyang, southwest of the modern city of Taiyuan, and the 'attacking cities and plundering towns' must have taken place inside that area. For contrast, the background figures: between the seventh and thirteenth years of Daye the Sui campaigned twice against Goguryeo, the histories speaking of hundreds of thousands of men levied and as many again of labourers, and Taiyuan was one of the mustering and grain-supply bases. Famine and pestilence followed the campaigns, and in the winter of the twelfth year the Sui Yangdi called up the soldiers of the empire for Liaodong a third time; the dead of the labour gangs filled the roads and the famine-stricken lay everywhere, and the households of the Taiyuan area bore this more directly than most. By the thirteenth year of Daye, Li Yuan had risen in the fifth month, had been advanced to Prince of Tang in the seventh, and Liu Wuzhou had entered Taiyuan at the year's end; and before the death of the Sui Yangdi at Jiangdu in the second year of Wude was known, with the Sui surviving in name only, the moment at which Yang Shiluo rose fell inside that window of collapsing order. The card's weapon is older still: a Roman heavy infantryman of about 100 BC, which had nothing to do with any of this.
cause: 起義的直接起因是隋末河東的秩序崩解，根子則在大業年間的全國性崩潰。太原郡是隋朝用兵西北與東北的基地之一：大業十一年征吐谷渾，十一年至十三年兩度征高句麗，太原都是出征、屯糧與轉運的樞紐；連年徵兵、徵役、徵糧，男子多為丁，農家失耕，丁壯大量流亡軍籍之外，民間怨望積累已深。高句麗戰役的敗績與天災疫癘相隨，隋煬帝又於大業十二年冬至十三年春第三次徵天下之兵於遼東，役死者填道，餓殍遍野，太原一帶的民戶承受尤其直接。到了大業十三年，隋室對地方的控制只剩下稅斛與徵發的權力：五月李淵在晉陽起兵，隋朝的太原守軍隨之易手，郡縣官吏與縣兵一時不知聽誰的號令；李淵入關後專力於關中與洛陽，對河東只剩一個大義的名分，李元吉的幕府既要籌措軍糧，又要防突厥與劉武周，能投入郡內平叛的兵力自然有限。就在這樣的權力真空裡，楊世洛以本郡人望號召鄉里，於十月聚眾起事；同年全國同時有李密、竇建德、梁師都、劉武周各據一方，隋朝的地方軍政單位彼此不再相屬，一支萬餘人的地方起義在河東腹心之地成形，正是這個大亂局最尋常的產物。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of the rising was the breakdown of order in Hedong, and the root of it lay in the collapse of the empire during the Daye years. The Taiyuan commandery was one of the Sui's bases for campaigning in the north-west and the north-east: in the eleventh year of Daye the court campaigned against the Tuyuhun, and between the eleventh and thirteenth years it campaigned twice against Goguryeo, and Taiyuan served each time as a point of mustering, of garrison farming and of grain transport. Levies, labour and grain were drawn from it year after year; men of military age were counted into the registers, the farmers lost their ploughing, and men drifted away from the registers in large numbers, and resentment had been accumulating for a long time. The defeat in Goguryeo was followed by famine and pestilence, and in the winter of the twelfth year and the spring of the thirteenth the Sui Yangdi called up the soldiers of the whole empire for Liaodong a third time, the dead of the labour gangs filling the roads and the famine-stricken lying everywhere; the households of the Taiyuan area bore this more directly than most. By the thirteenth year of Daye all that remained of the Sui's hold on the localities was the power to collect grain and to call up men. In the fifth month Li Yuan rose at Jinyang and the Sui garrison of Taiyuan changed hands with him, so that for a time the officers and the county troops of the commandery did not know whose orders to obey. After Li Yuan had entered Guanzhong he gave all his attention to Guanzhong and Luoyang and kept in Hedong nothing but a claim of righteousness, while Li Yuanji's staff had to raise grain, watch the Turks and watch Liu Wuzhou at the same time, and had few troops to send against a rising inside the commandery. It was into this vacuum of authority that Yang Shiluo, a man of local standing in his own commandery, called the villages of his home district and raised his men in the tenth month. In the same year Li Mi, Dou Jiande, Liang Shidu and Liu Wuzhou each held a part of the empire, the local military authorities of the Sui no longer answered to one another, and a local rising of ten thousand men taking shape in the heart of Hedong was the most ordinary product of that great disorder.
impact: 此役在正史留下的痕跡極薄，但可以確定的影響有兩層。第一層是眼前的：楊世洛在太原郡腹心之地聚起萬餘人、攻掠縣邑，等於在唐軍的大後方點了一處火；李元吉必須分兵應付，兵力和注意力被牽制，而同年冬天劉武周即乘虛引突厥之眾攻入太原、晉陽失守，兩件事在時間上緊接，說明河東的防守當時是多線受敵、彼此不能相顧。第二層是制度上的：地方起義能以「萬餘人」為量級在短期內成形，反映隋末的府兵制與縣兵制已失去編制與供應能力——兵在府而無糧、兵有籍而無械，一旦有人登高一呼，鬥志與物資便迅速匯集；而正史只記一筆的結果又顯示另一件事：在唐人編史的取捨裡，只有威脅到關中、洛陽與大河主流的勢力才會被寫進正史，純粹的地方民變往往被略過，乃至其首領連生卒年、籍貫之外的記載都付闕如。史載有限、諸說並存，這一場起義的實際規模、戰鬥經過與結局都無法從現存文獻中還原；把它當作隋末亂局中一環的標本來讀，比把它當作一場可考戰役更為恰當。
impactEn: The thinnest traces are left in the official record, but two kinds of consequence can be made out. The first is immediate: a rising of more than ten thousand men in the heart of Taiyuan commandery, attacking and plundering the county towns, was a fire lit in the rear of the Tang armies. Li Yuanji had to detach troops to answer it, and his strength and attention were divided; and in the winter of that same year Liu Wuzhou took advantage of the opening to bring Turkic forces into Taiyuan, and Jinyang was lost. The two events follow one another closely in time, and show that the defence of Hedong was being pressed from several lines at once and that the commanders could not help one another. The second is institutional: the fact that a local rising could reach a strength of 'more than ten thousand' within a short space of time shows that the fubing system and the county militia of the late Sui had lost both their muster and their supply, with soldiers on the register without grain and soldiers enrolled without arms, so that once someone raised the standard, courage and materiel came together very quickly. At the same time, the fact that the official histories give this rising only a single line shows something else: in the choices the Tang compilers made, only those powers that threatened Guanzhong, Luoyang and the main streams of the Yellow River were written into the record; purely local disturbances were passed over, and their leaders were left without even their dates of birth, to say nothing of their deeds. The records here are thin and the accounts conflict, and neither the real scale of this rising, nor the course of the fighting, nor its outcome can be restored from the surviving literature. It is better read as one specimen of the great disorder at the end of the Sui than as a battle whose course can be reconstructed.
result: 結果如何，正史沒有交代。兩《隋書》記到「聚眾萬餘人，攻城掠邑」便無下文，沒有記載楊世洛的敗亡、投降或被誅，也沒有留下官軍斬獲的數字，因此此役沒有可以確定的結局。其一說認為這是局限於郡內的短期民變，隨隋唐在河東的換手而自行潰散；其二說認為這股勢力為後來盤踞太原的劉武周所吸收，成為其進攻唐室的內應；其三說認為它在隋軍進剿下很快平定，領袖不過地方豪強的自保之舉。三說並無一說有直接文獻支持，也無一說能被現存史料排除，故此處只能存疑。真正可以確認的，是它在六一七年十月到年底這段時間裡確實使太原郡的部分縣城遭到攻掠，使唐方在河東的部署多了一處分散兵力的隱患，並把隋末「郡兵虛、府兵疲、倉廩空」的局面暴露在史冊上。回頭看卡面那件羅馬重步兵，可以確定的只有一句：它與太原郡無涉，沒有出現在任何一次隋末的戰鬥記載裡；而它所代表的兵制道理——重步兵的戰力不來自鎧甲本身，而來自兵源補充與補給線——恰好是隋唐府兵制的同一條教訓：兵再多，糧不繼，線一斷，烏合之眾再多也守不住城池。
resultEn: How it ended is not recorded. The two Histories of Sui stop at the words 'gathered more than ten thousand men, attacked cities and plundered towns' and say no more: there is no account of the defeat, surrender or execution of Yang Shiluo, and no figure for the government troops' captures, so this action has no ascertainable outcome. One account holds that it was a short-lived disturbance confined to the commandery that dissolved of itself as Sui and Tang changed hands in Hedong; another holds that the force was absorbed by Liu Wuzhou, who was later to hold Taiyuan, and became an accomplice of his advance against the Tang; a third holds that it was quickly put down by government troops and that its leader was no more than a local strongman acting to protect his own interests. None of the three has any direct documentary support, and none can be excluded on the strength of the surviving material, so the point must be left open. What can be confirmed is that between the tenth month of 617 and the end of that year the county towns of the commandery were in fact attacked and plundered, that the Tang deployment in Hedong was given one more reason to scatter its troops, and that the state of affairs in which 'the county troops were hollow, the fubing were exhausted and the granaries were empty' was laid bare in the histories. Looking back at the Roman heavy infantryman on the card, only one thing can be said with certainty: it had nothing to do with Taiyuan commandery, and it appears in no account of any fighting of the late Sui. And yet the military principle it stands for, that the strength of heavy infantry does not come from the armour but from the replenishment of men and from the supply line, is the same lesson the fubing system of Sui and Tang taught: no matter how many men are gathered, if the grain does not come and the line is broken, no mass, however large, can hold a city.
